why: Area of lines i < j is min(h[i], h[j]) * (j - i). Start with the widest pair; the shorter line can never do better with a narrower partner, so discard it by moving that pointer inward. That is the opposite-ends two-pointer squeeze.
hints: Checking every pair is O(n^2). Start at the widest container, both ends. Which line limits its area?
The shorter of the two ends caps the height. Any other container using that short line is narrower and no taller, so that line is finished: move its pointer inward.
Two pointers i = 0, j = n-1; record the area, move the shorter side, stop when they meet. O(n) time, O(1) space.
pitfalls: On equal heights, moving either pointer is safe.
Width is j - i (index distance), not the count of lines.
constraints:
• 2 <= height.length <= 10^5
  • 0 <= height[i] <= 10^4
  • Bounds not stated in the source; these are the standard ones.
